title: A study testing a weight management programme for adults with cystic fibrosis
official: A randomised feasibility study to test a cystic fibrosis specific weight management programme alongside an NHS digital weight management programme (MoreLife®-CF) compared to delivering an NHS digital weight management programme only (MoreLife®) in adults with cystic fibrosis (the MoreLife®-CF feasibility study)
summary:
Background and study aims 
Cystic fibrosis (CF) is a life-limiting genetic condition that affects the lungs and digestive system. People with CF were encouraged to eat a high-calorie diet because gaining weight was difficult and being well nourished helps them stay healthier. New treatments have now improved their health, but some adults with CF are becoming overweight or obese and they now require support to manage their weight.
This study will test whether it is feasible to deliver a CF-specific digital weight management programme (MoreLife® CF) alongside an NHS digital weight management programme (MoreLife®). We want to understand whether the study design and the MoreLife® CF programme can be delivered in CF services, whether it is more acceptable, useful and interesting to people with CF than the NHS MoreLife® only, and whether a future larger trial would be possible.

Who can participate? 
Patients aged 18 years and over with CF who are overweight or obese

What does the study involve? 
Participants will be allocated by chance into two groups: one group will receive MoreLife® CF and the other will receive the NHS MoreLife® only. The study will last 16 weeks. Before and after taking part in the programmes, participants will have their height, weight, waist, body composition and handgrip strength measured. They will complete some questionnaires about their wellbeing, knowledge and approach to behaviour change. They will also record what they eat, and wear an activity monitor. At the end of the study, participants and the dietitians who delivered the programmes will be invited to interviews to share their views on taking part and how acceptable and engaging they found the study procedures and the MoreLife® CF programme.

What are the possible benefits and risks of participating? 
Taking part in this study may help adults with CF learn new ways to manage their diet, weight and physical activity. It will also provide them with access to useful educational resources about healthy eating and physical activity suitable for adults with CF. Participation in the study will also help researchers improve future weight management support for adults with cystic fibrosis.
Taking part will require time and commitment, and some people may find discussing their experiences or completing study activities emotionally challenging. The programme aims to support healthy weight loss, but any concerns about weight loss, physical and mental health, or wellbeing will be monitored by the participants CF team. Adults with CF who are pregnant are not eligible to participate. Continued participation will be reviewed if they become pregnant during the study.

Where is the study run from? 
University of Birmingham (UK)

When is the study starting and how long is it expected to run for? 
March 2027 to March 2028

Who is funding the study? 
National Institute for Health and Care Research (NIHR) (UK)

Who is the main contact?
Joanne Barrett, joanne.barrett2@nhs.net

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Registered at recruiting site
2. Confirmed diagnosis of CF with genotype
3. Clinically stable (no respiratory exacerbation within previous) 28 days
4. Aged >18 years
5. Body mass index (BMI) >25 kg/m2
6. Prescribed or self-funded GIP-1, GIP dual receptor agonist medications for weight loss or diabetes management, e.g., tirzepatide,semaglutide
7. Digital smartphone and web access
8. Able to give informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
1. Pregnant
2. Diagnosis of an eating disorder 
3. Currently a hospital inpatient 
4. Currently being screened for cystic fibrosis–related diabetes (CFRD) using flash glucose monitoring at time of recruitment
5. Currently receiving treatment for distal intestinal obstruction syndrome (DIOS) or acute constipation at time of recruitment
6. Currently receiving oral or IV antibiotics for respiratory exacerbation at time of recruitment
7. Currently prescribed an increased dose of glucocorticoid (above usual maintenance dose) at time of recruitment
